rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the pronoun in ‘in them’ back to all twelve months, since wrongdoing is forbidden in every month, not only the four sacred ones.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم عوده على الاثنى عشر أيضا بل هو الصواب لأنه لا يجوز أن ينهى عن الظلم في الأربعة ويبيح الظلم في الثمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers taking the pronoun back to the four sacred months: injustice is wrong generally but especially heinous in them.
rows.anchor: قلت لكن يجوز التنصيص على افضلية الحرم فإن الظلم قبيح مطلقا وفيهن اقبح فالظاهر الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A demonstrative can take the place of a pronoun, as ‘all those’ gathers hearing, sight, and heart under one reference.
rows.anchor: كل أولئك كان عنه مسؤولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article can stand in for a pronoun: Hell is its refuge for the one who preferred worldly life, while Paradise is the refuge for the one who feared God.
rows.anchor: فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans explain the definite article in these refuge phrases as a substitute for the omitted pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقول الكوفيين الألف واللام عوض من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘we answer Your call and follow the messengers,’ the article in ‘the messengers’ supplies the possessive sense ‘Your messengers.’
rows.anchor: نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general noun ‘the virtuous’ replaces a pronoun: although the sense starts as ‘his reward and patience,’ the individual is included in that class.
rows.anchor: أصل الكلام أجره وصبره ولما كان المحسنون جنسا ومن يتق ويصبر واحد تحته أغنى عمومه من عود الضمير إليه

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik applies the article-as-pronoun analysis to ‘the doors’ in ‘gardens of Eden, whose doors are opened for them.’
rows.anchor: قال ابن مالك وعليه يحمل قوله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analyzes ‘the doors’ as an apposition to the implicit subject of ‘opened.’
rows.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري ( 6 ) إن الأبواب بدل من المستكن في مفتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the apposition as strained: the stated or an implied ‘opened’ can govern ‘the doors’ directly.
rows.anchor: وهذا تكلف فوجب إن تكون الأبواب مرتفعة بمفتحة المذكور أو بمثله مقدرا وقد صح إن مفتحة صالح للعمل في الأبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A context that calls for a pronoun may instead use an explicit noun; the author refers readers to his earlier discussion under emphasis.
rows.anchor: ومنها الاسم الظاهر بأن يكون المقام يقتضي الإضمار فيعدل عنه إلى الظاهر وقد سبق الكلام عليه في أبواب التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun normally refers to the nearest preceding noun, but after a construct it refers to the head noun, the topic, rather than its genitive complement.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الضمير عوده إلى أقرب مذكور ولنا أصل آخر وهو أنه إذا جاء مضاف ومضاف إليه وذكر بعدهما ضمير عاد إلى المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘you cannot count it’ refers to the construct’s head, ‘blessing,’ rather than to ‘God.’
rows.anchor: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans supply the omitted complement as ‘it is his refuge.’
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن الإضمار بعدها مراد وإنما اختلفوا في تقديره فعند الكوفيين هي مأواه

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans supply the omitted complement as ‘it is the refuge for him.’
rows.anchor: وعند البصريين هي المأوى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The article’s lām is normally light; in the name Allah it is emphatic after a preceding fatḥa or ḍamma, conveying reverence for God.
rows.anchor: واللام في التعريف مرققة إلا في اسم الله فيجب تفخيمها إذا كان قبلها ضمة أو فتحة وهي في الأسماء تفخيم الجرس وفي المعنى توقير المسمى وتعظيمه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in demonstrative names signals distance or reinforces it; grammarians differ on which function it has.
rows.anchor: والدالة على البعد الداخلة على أسماء الإشارة إعلاما بالبعد أو توكيدا له على الخلاف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With weakened inna, the lām is called the initial or differentiating lām because it distinguishes the affirmative particle from negative inna and confirms the predicate.
rows.anchor: وتسمى لام الابتداء والفارقة لأنها تفرق بينها وبين إن النافية والمخففة هي التي تحقق الخبر مع المبتدأ

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans take lām to mean ‘except’ in affirmative clauses, with inna meaning ‘not’; al-Kisa’i reads the verb with the nominative on this basis.
rows.anchor: والموجبة بمعنى إلا عند الكوفيين

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i reads ‘to make the mountains disappear’ in the nominative and understands the clause as ‘their plot was only intended to make them disappear.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ﴿ وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال ﴾ 6 بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphatic lām can precede a subject or occur with inna on a delayed subject or predicate; inna emphasizes what follows and lām emphasizes the predicate.
rows.anchor: أحدهما المبتدأ وتسمى لام الابتداء فيؤذن بأنه المحكوم

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa‘id reads the hamza of inna open in ‘they surely eat’; the author explains that its lām is licensed only with kasra-inna or with a fronted predicate.
rows.anchor: وكذا في إن المفتوحة كقراءة سعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a predicate precedes inna, the lām can attach to the fronted phrase; the underlying order is ‘they wander in their intoxication.’
rows.anchor: أو على ما يتصل بالخبر إذا تقدم عليه

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi supplies ‘entry into’ or ‘abiding in’ gardens: glad tidings is an abstract noun, so it cannot be predicated directly of the concrete gardens.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي التقدير بشراكم دخول جنات أو خلود جنات لان البشرى مصدر والجنات ذات فلا يخبر بالذات عن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name for the utterance can stand for what was uttered: ‘what they say’ means the content of their claim, and ‘what they said’ means the thing alleged.
rows.anchor: أي عن مدلول قولهم ومنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ‘name’ can stand for the named being: ‘glorify the name of your Lord’ means glorify your Lord.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الاسم على المسمى كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘A word from Him’ refers by trope to Jesus, who came into being through God’s word without a father; his being honored and near to God proves the referent is a person.
rows.anchor: تجوز بالكلمة عن المسيح لكونه تكون بها من غير أب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘his name is the Messiah,’ the pronoun refers to the referent of ‘word,’ while ‘name’ means the person named: the announced one is the Messiah son of Mary.
rows.anchor: فإن الضمير فيه عائد إلى مدلول الكلمة والمراد بالاسم المسمى فالمعنى المسمى المبشر به المسيح بن مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Your oaths’ can mean the object sworn by, God: do not make an oath in God’s name prevent you from doing good and reconciling people.
rows.anchor: أي لاتجعلوا يمين الله أو قسم الله مانعا لما تحلفون عليه من البر والتقوى بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here desire stands for the sins the self desires; forbidding inclination itself is impossible, so the phrase means forbidding the self from following desire.
rows.anchor: أي عما تهواه من المعاصي ولا يصح نهيها عن هواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Secretly’ is a trope for intercourse because it usually occurs in private, then for a marriage contract because intercourse results from it; the verse forbids contracting marriage during the waiting period.
rows.anchor: فإنه مجاز عن مجاز

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority of the Muslim community holds that emphasis occurs in the Qur’an and Sunna.
rows.anchor: الأولى جمهور الأمة على وقوعه في القرآن والسنة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some deny that emphasis exists in the Qur’an, Sunna, or language, insisting that each expression must add a new meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم ليس فيهما تأكيد ولا في اللغة بل لابد أن يفيد معنى زائدا على الأول

rows.speaker: الملحدون
rows.claim: Critics call emphasis pointless repetition and argue that eloquence requires concise wording; they suppose it reflects inability to express the intended meaning otherwise.
rows.anchor: واعترض الملحدون على القرآن والسنة

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: The defenders answer that the Qur’an speaks in the Arabs’ language, where emphasis and repetition are recognized parts of eloquence and have many benefits.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الأصحاب بأن القرآن نزل على لسان القوم وفي لسانهم التأكيد والتكرار وخطابه أكثر بل هو عندهم معدود في الفصاحة والبراعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says denial of emphasis in language is untenable: otherwise the term would have no known referent, and emphasis has many benefits.
rows.anchor: بل فوائد كثيرة كما سنبينه

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some classify emphasis as figurative because it contributes no meaning beyond the first expression; al-Tartusi records this position.
rows.anchor: وزعم قوم انه نجاز لأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author holds emphasis to be literal: if the second identical ‘hurry’ were figurative, the first would be too, which is impossible because it precedes it.
rows.anchor: جاز في الاول لانهما في لفظ واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis goes against the default reading, so a word should be parsed as emphatic only when an independent meaning cannot be assigned to it.
rows.anchor: إنه خلاف الأصل فلا يحمل اللفظ على التأكيد إلا عند تعذر حمله على مدة محددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects an unspecified criterion that accepts any meaning, since the meaning conveyed by a word is not itself another word-form that must imitate it.
rows.anchor: وما قاله ضعيف لأن المفهوم من دلالة اللفظ ليس من باب الألفاظ حتى يحذو به حذو الألفاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Technical emphasis divides into verbal and semantic forms; verbal emphasis restates the first meaning with the same word or a synonym.
rows.anchor: القسم الأول التوكيد الصناعي وهو قسمان لفظي ومعنوي فاللفظي تقرير معنى الأول بلفظ أو مرادفه

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar treats ‘in it as broad roads’ as synonym-based verbal emphasis; he also classifies ‘in whatever We established you’ this way if both particles are negative.
rows.anchor: وجعل الصفار منه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative ‘taqāt’ has three parses depending on sense: verbal noun of guarding, object meaning something to avoid, or a plural like ‘noble men’ and ‘archers’ used circumstantially.
rows.anchor: فى نصبها ثلاثة أوجه مبنية على تفسيرها

rows.speaker: أحد القولين
rows.claim: One interpretation takes ‘aḥwā’ as blackened by drying and withering.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه الأسود من الجفاف واليبس

rows.speaker: الثاني
rows.claim: The opposing interpretation takes ‘aḥwā’ as black from intense greenness, as in ‘both dark green gardens.’
rows.anchor: والثانى أنه الأسود من شدة الخضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the dryness reading it modifies the refuse; on the greenness reading it is circumstantial of the pasture, and is delayed to suit the verse endings.
rows.anchor: فعلى الأول هو صفة لغثاء وعلى الثاني هو حال من المرعى وأخر لتناسب الفواصل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes ‘kifāt’ as containers and ‘living and dead’ as referring to what grows and what does not; those words modify the containers or are circumstantial.
rows.anchor: فإنه قيل الكفات الأوعية ومفردها كفت والأحياء والأموات كناية عما نبت وما لا ينبت وقيل الكفات مصدر كفته إذا ضمه وجمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ‘kifāt’ means containers, ‘living and dead’ describes them or is circumstantial; if it is a verbal noun, both are objects of an omitted verb meaning ‘gathers.’
rows.anchor: صفة لكفاتا كأنه قيل أوعية حية وميتة أو حالان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ‘the seven oft-repeated’ means the Qur’an, ‘from’ is partitive and the phrase puts the general after the specific; if it means the Fātiḥa, ‘from’ explains the kind.
rows.anchor: فمن للتبعيض والقرآن حينئذ من عطف العام على الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies ‘cursed be man, how ungrateful he is’ as divine expression of wonder, alongside ‘how patient they are over the Fire’ and ‘how clearly He sees and hears.’
rows.anchor: التعجب الواقع في كلام الله نحو

words: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the heavens and earth do not end, the permanence formula follows Arab custom, which uses their duration to express eternity in both reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: مع أنهما لايزولان لكن التقييد بالسماء والأرض جرت عادة العرب إذا قصدوا الدوام أن يعلقوا بهما فجاء الخطاب على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context determines whether a question conveys exaltation or belittlement: the next verse’s ‘from a drop He created him’ makes ‘from what thing?’ belittling.
rows.anchor: وكما فهم التحقير من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may imply equivalence without stating it explicitly, as in ‘whether what you are promised is near or far.’
rows.anchor: وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative ‘who is it that can intercede?’ serves to magnify God’s authority, since intercession is possible only by His permission.
rows.anchor: من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated questions can intimidate or magnify an event; ‘what do the criminals hasten?’ magnifies the punishment they seek to hasten.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون ﴾ 3 تفخيم للعذاب الذي يستعجلونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An interrogative can ease or minimize the perceived burden, as in ‘what would it cost them if they believed in God?’
rows.anchor: وماذا عليهم لو آمنوا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An interrogative can express grief, as in the complaint that the record leaves out neither small nor great deed.
rows.anchor: ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative ‘how many a town’ can express abundance or multitude.
rows.anchor: وكم من قرية أهلكناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ question is apparently a request for guidance, with its phrasing shaped by etiquette; another view takes it as wonder.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنهم استفهموا مسترشدين وإنما فرق بين العبارتين أدبا وقيل هي هنا للتعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogatives can function as performative speech acts, including commands; for example, ‘will you not reflect?’ means ‘reflect.’
rows.anchor: القسم الثاني الاستفهام المراد به الإنشاء وهو على ضروب الأول مجرد الطلب وهو الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interrogatives enact commands: submit, love forgiveness, fight, reflect on the Qur’an, or desist; Umar answered the last ‘we desist.’
rows.anchor: وقل للذين أوتوا الكتاب والأميين أأسلمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ‘what has beguiled you by your generous Lord?’ functions as a prohibition: do not let anything beguile you.
rows.anchor: الثاني النهي كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do you fear them?’ functions as a prohibition against fearing people, confirmed by the command not to fear people in 5:44.
rows.anchor: أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some also classify ‘do you not know that God is capable of all things?’ as an interrogative that commands belief or recognition.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعضهم منه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية والزمخشري
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari read ‘will you be patient?’ as asking whether they will endure or not.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية والزمخشري المعنى اتصبرون أم لا تصبرون

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani supplies an omitted phrase, ‘so that We may know whether you endure,’ for the question ‘will you be patient?’
rows.anchor: والجرجاني في النظم على حذف مضاف أي لنعلم اتصبرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited pairs, sīn denotes limited or partial breadth while emphatic ṣād conveys full breadth; the author links this sense to ṣād’s emphatic articulation.
rows.anchor: فبالسين السعة الجزئية كذلك علة التقييد وبالصاد السعة الكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīn in ‘sūra’ marks something that encloses an object from outside, while ṣād in ‘ṣūra’ marks what contains it within.
rows.anchor: فبالسين ما يحصر الشيء خارجا عنه وبالصاد ما تضمنه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sīn in ‘they conceal’ is from secrecy, while ṣād in ‘they persist’ conveys continued insistence.
rows.anchor: فبالسين من السر وبالصاد من التمادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīn in ‘they are dragged’ denotes pulling, whereas ṣād in ‘they are accompanied’ denotes companionship.
rows.anchor: فبالسين من الجر وبالصاد من الصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīn in the division of provision signals allotting blessings; ṣād in ‘how many We destroyed’ signals division through annihilation.
rows.anchor: بالسين تفريق الأرزاق والإنعام وبالصاد تفريق الإهلاك والإعدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces described with ḍād enjoy what souls desire, whereas those described with ẓāʾ enjoy what eyes delight in.
rows.anchor: منعمة بما تشتهيه الأنفس وبالظاء منعمة بما تلذ الأعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noun indicates a stable, continuing quality: ‘spreading his forelegs’ describes the dog’s settled posture, whereas the verb would suggest a newly undertaken action.
rows.anchor: لو قيل يبسط لم يؤد الغرض لأنه لم يؤذن بمزاولة الكلب البسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ‘provides for you’ conveys provision renewed piece by piece; replacing it with the noun ‘provider’ would lose that sense.
rows.anchor: لو قيل رازقكم لفات ما افاده الفعل من تجدد الرزق شيئا بعد شئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A present verb in a circumstantial phrase depicts action underway at the time of arrival and renewing moment by moment, as in ‘they came to their father weeping.’
rows.anchor: إذ المراد إن يريد صورة ما هم عليه وقت المجئ وأنهم آخذون في البكاء يجددونه شيئا بعد شئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending is described with a verb because it is an action that stops and recurs; faith, piety, patience, gratitude, guidance, and similar states can be named as lasting qualities.
rows.anchor: لأن حقيقة النفقة أمر فعلي شأنه الانقطاع والتجدد بخلاف الإيمان فإن له حقيقة تقوم بالقلب يدوم مقتضاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nouns such as ‘strivers,’ ‘emigrants,’ and ‘believers’ can stress established traits rooted in the heart, even where the corresponding deeds recur.
rows.anchor: كالمجاهدين والمهاجرين والمؤمنين لأنه للشان والصفة هذا مع إن لها في القلوب أصولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s guidance or misguidance as an act appears in verb constructions, while ‘a guide for every people’ names a stable role.
rows.anchor: لطيفة وهو إن ما كان من شأنه ألا يفعل إلا مجازاة وليس من شأنه أن يذكر الاتصاف به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation says Mary’s community performed prostration before bowing; another takes the bowing as the bow of the second rakʿa.
rows.anchor: قيل يحتمل أنه كان في شريعتهم السجود قبل الركوع ويحتمل أن يراد بالركوع ركوع الركعة الثانية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the command ‘bow’ as ‘give thanks.’
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد ب اركعي اشكري

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes ‘prostrate’ as praying alone and ‘bow with those who bow’ as praying in congregation.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد ب اسجدي صلي وحدك وب اركعي صلي في جماعة

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says the order follows the Prophet’s own recognition: belief in God, then Jibril, the revealed book, and finally his own prophethood; the sequence tracks how revelation was received.
rows.anchor: ذكره السهيلي في آماليه

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another writer sees a sequence from the source of mercy, God, through the angels who convey it and the books that embody it, to the prophets who receive it.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره في هذا الترتيب سر لطيف

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة محمد بن بحر الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Abu Salama argues that ‘weighed’ is more general than ‘measured’: measured goods become weighed when divided, and weighing also expresses the equality and adjustment sought in measuring.
rows.anchor: قال أبو سلمة محمد بن بحر الأصبهاني في تفسيره إنما خص الموزون بالذكر دون المكيل لأمرين أحدهما أن غاية المكيل ينتهي إلى الموزون

rows.speaker: الشريف المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Sharif al-Murtada rejects that explanation: ‘weighed’ means apportioned to need, neither deficient nor harmfully excessive.
rows.anchor: وقال الشريف المرتضى في الغرر 1 هذا خلاف المقصود بل المراد بالموزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ‘year’ for Noah’s long ordeal and ‘years’ for the exception suggests hardship throughout except for fifty years of relief; ‘year’ commonly names drought and famine.
rows.anchor: فذكر في مدة اللبث السنة وفي الانفصال العام للإشارة إلى أنه كان في شدائد في مدته كلها

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli suggests the wording reflects a lifespan of a thousand years in which the fifty were lunar years, about a year and a half shorter than fifty solar years.
rows.anchor: قال السهيلي ويجوز أن يكون الله سبحانه قد علم أن عمره كان ألفا إلا أن الخمسين منها كانت أعواما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrases ‘fifty thousand years’ and ‘a thousand years by your reckoning’ amplify and complete the duration; the source distinguishes the longer sana from ʿām.
rows.anchor: كلام ورد في موضع التكثير والتتميم بمدة ذلك اليوم والسنة أطول من العام

rows.speaker: ابن الزملكاني
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zamalkani counts blended coinages such as ‘ḥawqala’ and ‘basmala’ among Quranic inimitability; he analyzes ‘God suffices as witness’ as combining ‘sufficed him’ with ‘be content with Him,’ making it both report and command.
rows.anchor: جعله ابن الزملكاني من 1 نظوم القرآن ومثله بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘suffices as witness,’ ‘witness’ is parsed as specification or a circumstantial accusative, with the phrase carrying both an assertion and an imperative to rely on God.
rows.anchor: وكذلك انتصب شهديا على التمييز أو الحال

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik cites ‘ask the people of the Reminder’ as an inserted clause between ‘We revealed to them’ and ‘with clear proofs and scriptures,’ challenging Abu Ali’s limit of one parenthetical sentence.
rows.anchor: وبهذه الآية ابن مالك على أبي علي الفارسي قوله إنه لا يعترض بأكثر من جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians treat the command as evidence for the answer to the condition, while others treat it as the answer itself; either way the command and condition form one sentence.
rows.anchor: ورد بأن جملة الأمر دليل للجواب عند الأكثرين ونفسه عند آخرين فهو مع جملة الشرط كالجملة الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ‘reclining on couches’ is a circumstantial phrase from ‘whoever fears his Lord has two gardens,’ the interruption totals seven sentences when ‘with branches’ is a predicate, otherwise six.
rows.anchor: فلزم الاعتراض بسبع جمل مستقلات

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari is reported to count seven inserted sentences in the passage about towns’ faith, blessings, denial, and punishment, and to connect ‘did the people feel secure?’ to ‘We seized them.’
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik says the count of four interruptions comes from treating ‘sentence’ and ‘utterance’ as synonyms, and counts the entire conditional unit as one because its meaning completes only as a whole.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مالك ورد عليه من ظن أن الجملة والكلام مترادفان قال وإنما اعترض بأربع جمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recalculates eight interruptions: ‘while unaware,’ the four elements of the conditional clause, ‘but they denied,’ ‘We seized them,’ and ‘for what they used to earn.’
rows.anchor: أما على قول ابن مالك فينبغي أن يكون بعدها ثمان جمل أحدها

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr argues that if eloquent opponents had thought the Qur’an was poetry, they would have challenged it, since poetry was accessible; their failure shows they did not regard it as poetry.
rows.anchor: فالجواب قال القاضي أبو بكر إن الفصحاء منهم

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: It is implausible that the masters of Arabic rhetoric missed poetry in the Qur’an while later readers detected it, given their strong motive to discredit it.
rows.anchor: فمن استدرك فيه شعرا زعم أنه خفي على أولئك النفر وهم ملوك الكلام

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل صناعة العربية
rows.claim: Most Muslim Arabic specialists say a single metrical line is not poetry; poetry requires at least two lines, and two lines with different meters and rhymes are not poetry.
rows.anchor: وقالوا أيضا إن ما كان على وزن بيتين إلا أنه يختلف وزنهما وقافيتهما فليس بشعر أصلا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some deny that rajaz is poetry, especially when it is a half-line or fragment; others require at least four rajaz lines, which the Qur’an does not contain.
rows.anchor: ثم منهم من قال إن الرلجز ليس بشعر أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry requires deliberate use of a poetic method; accidental meter in ordinary speech does not make every speaker a poet.
rows.anchor: ثم يقول إن الشعر إنما ينطلق متى قصد إليه على الطريق التي تعمد وتسلك ولا يصح أن يتفق مثله إلا من الشعراء

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr considers this defense reliable or mostly so and adds that people would naturally try to rival poetry, which is not intractable for contemporaries.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي وهذه الطريق التي سلكوها في الجواب معتمدة أو أكثرها ولو كان ذلك شعرا لكانت النفوس تتشوق إلى معارضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A facet of inimitability is varying register and placing the wording suited to each situation; replacing a word with a synonym removes its elegance and sweetness.
rows.anchor: مما يبعث على معرفة الإعجاز اختلافات المقامات وذكر في كل موضع ما يلائمه
